 Pascal Siakam 
 IND 
 Forward 
 #43 
 Player Stats
 Link copied to clipboard! 
 Pascal Siakam amassed 19 points (5-of-13 FGs, 7-of-12 FTs), three rebounds, two assists and two three-pointers in Friday’s win over the Knicks.
 The ending wasn’t pretty for Siakam, who missed two free throws with 23.4 seconds left, which could have extended Indiana’s lead to six, and then committed a turnover with five seconds left, giving New York one final chance to tie. While he shot 2-of-4 from beyond the arc, Siakam went 3-of-9 from two and finished with more turnovers (three) than assists (two). He’ll look to end the week on a high note when the Pacers visit the 76ers on Sunday. 
 -  Raphielle Johnson

 Pascal Siakam scores 28 points (7-of-17 FGs, 12-of-12 FTs), eight rebounds, five assists, a steal, and two 3’s in the 114-101 win against the Wizards. 
 Siakam helped lead the Pacers past the Wizards with this one and his scoring was much needed in this game. His ability to get to the line in this game was crucial. He helped them stay in the game in the first half. Pascal from a fantasy perspective has been very consistent. He won’t do this every game, but it’s nice when it happens. The 12-12 from the free throw line is a really nice bump at this point in the week. 
 Pascal Siakam 
 IND 
 Forward 
 #43 
 Pascal Siakam amassed a team-high 29 points (9-of-16 FGs, 6-of-8 FTs), nine rebounds, eight assists and two steals over 35 minutes in Monday’s loss to the Mavericks. 
 Siakam came within one board and two assists of a triple-double, but it wasn’t enough to overcome a herculean performance by Dallas star Cooper Flagg. He knocked down 5-of-8 from three-point range and fell one-point shy of matching his previous season-high mark that he set during Indiana’s season opener against the Pelicans. The 32-year-old forward has delivered seventh-round fantasy value this season, averaging a robust 22.2 points, 6.8 rebounds, 4.3 assists, 1.0 steals and 0.1 blocks through 10 games.

 Pascal Siakam accumulated 23 points (10-of-18 FGs, 1-of-2 FTs), two rebounds, five assists and two three-pointers in Saturday’s loss to the Nuggets. 
 Siakam has scored at least 20 points in seven of nine games this season, including Saturday’s effort in Mexico City. Unfortunately, the Pacers forward’s production hasn’t led to wins, as Indiana has lost five of its last six games since Tyrese Haliburton suffered a strained hamstring. Siakam and the Pacers play four games next week, starting with the Mavericks on Monday.

 Pascal Siakam tallied 17 points (6-of-14 FGs, 5-of-6 FTs), five rebounds, five assists and one steal in Sunday’s loss to the Nets. 
 In the three games the Pacers have played since losing Tyrese Haliburton to a hamstring strain, Siakam has averaged 18.7 points per game while shooting 45.8 percent from the field. That isn’t necessarily bad, but not sharing the floor with a lead guard as talented as Haliburton lowers Siakam’s ceiling. On Sunday, he scored just four points in the second half, shooting 1-of-3 from the field. The Pacers play three games next week, starting with the Hawks on Monday.

 Pascal Siakam shot 5-of-17 from the field and 3-of-5 from the foul line in Friday’s loss to the Heat, scoring 13 points with five rebounds, four assists and two steals. 
 After a stellar showing on Wednesday in Indiana’s first game since losing Tyrese Haliburton to a hamstring strain, Siakam was held in check by the Timberwolves. He missed all five three-point attempts, which hurt his overall field-goal percentage. Haliburton doesn’t have a firm return timeline, but the Pacers will rely even more on Siakam in their point guard’s absence. Nights like Friday won’t become the norm for Siakam, but no Haliburton is a big deal.

Pascal did his best to lead the Pacers without Haliburton in this game and did a good job scoring the ball. He was a monster on the boards as the Pacers out hustled the 76ers in this game. We have at least two weeks before Haliburton comes back, so sit back and enjoy the production but also recognize that it might come down a bit once Haliburton comes back.

 Mikal Bridges amassed 18 points (8-of-12 FGs), three rebounds, three assists, two steals and two three-pointers in Friday’s loss to the Pacers.
 Much has been made of Bridges’ offensive struggles and with good reason, as he’s been in “spectator mode” in the fourth quarter of multiple games. That wasn’t the case on Friday, as the Knicks’ wing saw a few go down early and played well throughout. After playing 17 minutes in each of the Knicks’ two previous games, Bridges played 29 minutes on Friday. This performance came at a good time, as more fantasy managers have been deciding whether to hold onto Bridges or drop him.

 Karl-Anthony Towns recorded 23 points (9-of-19 FGs, 2-of-3 FTs), 15 rebounds, five assists, three steals and three three-pointers in Friday’s loss to the Pacers.
 Towns has now recorded a double-double in each of the Knicks’ first 12 games, breaking the franchise record for the longest double-double streak to begin a season, previously held by Willis Reed. He had a chance to force overtime, but his fadeaway fell short as time expired. Along with Jalen Brunson, Towns has been one of the few constants for the Knicks in their 6-6 start. He’ll look to extend his double-double streak on Sunday against the Raptors. 
 -  Raphielle Johnson

 Jalen Brunson accumulated 33 points (11-of-22 FGs, 7-of-8 FTs), one rebound, 11 assists, two steals and four three-pointers in Friday’s loss to the Pacers.
 With some of his teammates struggling offensively, Brunson once again shouldered the offensive workload on Friday. Despite being hounded by multiple defenders throughout the 106-104 defeat, the Knicks’ guard shot 50 percent from the field and posted double-digit assists for the first time this season. Brunson did finish with four turnovers, but the overall production compensated for that.

 Quenton Jackson (ankle) finished Friday’s win over the Knicks with three points (1-of-4 FGs), five rebounds, four assists, one steal and one three-pointer.
 Plus/minus is an imperfect stat and one that doesn’t factor into fantasy basketball. However, Jackson’s plus-22 led all players who saw action in Friday’s game. He had some solid defensive possessions, and his rebounding and assist production were good for those rostering him in dynasty leagues. Jackson appeared to tweak his right ankle on the final defensive possession but was walking fine after a brief moment sitting on the court. If Aaron Nesmith (hand) misses time, Jackson could return to the Pacers’ starting lineup. 
 -  Raphielle Johnson

 Andrew Nembhard recorded 12 points (4-of-14 FGs, 3-of-3 FTs), four rebounds, six assists and one three-pointer in Friday’s win over the Knicks.
 Nembhard has dished out at least six assists in four straight appearances, but the efficiency was lacking on Friday. The Pacers’ point guard committed six turnovers and shot poorly from the field, with a 1-of-6 night from three as the main culprit. T.J. McConnell (6/3/6/2) played a season-high 17 minutes off the bench, and as his minutes increase, that may help Nembhard by taking some playmaking responsibilities off his plate while Tyrese Haliburton (hamstring) is out.
